public_rationale: Nature reported on 22 April 2026 that hallucinations persisted in leading language models [e1]. This supports the concern about reliability but does not establish that solving it requires entirely new branches of mathematics [e1]. A preprint submitted that day reported reliability guarantees using established conformal prediction, with experiments on two benchmark datasets [e2]. Those results do not establish dependable general factual output using existing mathematics [e2]. Neither item meets the contract's requirement for an independently validated general solution, so the necessity forecast remains unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: Persistent hallucinations do not establish which mathematical foundations a solution would require [e1].
The preprint's two-dataset evaluation does not establish general reliability, useful answer coverage and appropriate abstention across diverse unfamiliar questions [e2].

criteria.support_condition: A broadly validated solution depends indispensably on genuinely new mathematical fields, with evidence establishing necessity rather than merely showing that new mathematics was used.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A broadly validated solution makes factual LLM output dependable using established mathematics and engineering, without requiring a new mathematical field.

evidence.explanation: The paper reports continuing hallucination and analyzes incentives using learning theory. Persistence supports concern about reliability but does not prove that a new mathematical field is required.

This offers a route to improved reliability through an existing statistical framework. Its two-dataset evaluation and bounded-error approach do not establish a general solution meeting the early-resolution rule.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An independently validated general solution with dependable factual performance, useful answer coverage and appropriate abstention across diverse tasks, including unfamiliar questions. Its documented foundations must establish either successful reliance on existing mathematics or the indispensable need for genuinely new mathematical fields.
